title: TLS-safe mode design is correct and the documented rationale is complete
description: The TLS-safe mode (cfg->tls_safe prevents hardware hash dispatch for TLS devIds) solves a real problem correctly: TLS 1.3 calls wc_Sha256Copy() for transcript hashing and hardware hash cannot snapshot in-flight state. The alternative — returning CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE for COPY when devCtx is non-null — is also present in the WOLF_CRYPTO_CB_COPY handler, but that would cause WC_HW_E if TLS 1.3 tries to copy a hash mid-update. The per-devId scoping (tls_safe is per-registered-devId, not global) correctly allows a separate bulk-data devId to use hardware hash. The port.h comment explaining WHY is comprehensive and would prevent a future contributor from naively re-enabling hardware hash for TLS. This is the right design. A future contributor might suggest 'just use hardware hash and implement COPY via a second Init+Replay' — which is wrong because the replay would require buffering all hash input, turning O(1) memory per hash into O(N) — worse than the current HMAC accumulation approach.
